llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent for Aliyun OSS deployment, but it reads stored GitHub credentials and can make production cloud, DNS, certificate, and GitHub Actions changes with broad triggers.

dimensions.detail: The scripts use Aliyun and GitHub APIs in line with the stated purpose, but set_github_secret.py and SKILL.md explicitly fall back to reading ~/.git-credentials instead of requiring an explicit scoped token.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is ordinary git clone or zip placement into a skill directory; I found no install-time hooks, package substitution, or hidden installer behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation phrases include generic deployment, launch, domain, and HTTPS wording that could match tasks outside Aliyun OSS, while the workflow can change public bucket access, DNS records, certificates, and repository Actions settings.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The certificate manager stores ACME account/certificate material under ~/.acme-oss and the docs recommend daily scheduled renewal; that is disclosed, but it is persistent credential/key material tied to cloud mutation authority.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently describe static-site deployment to Aliyun OSS, public access setup, custom-domain HTTPS, certificate renewal, and GitHub Actions secret/variable management; those are high-impact but purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only with a test bucket or test domain first, provide a dedicated least-privilege Aliyun RAM user, and avoid letting it read ~/.git-credentials; set an explicit, fine-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN instead. Confirm every operation that changes public bucket access, DNS, certificates, repository secrets, or scheduled renewal.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the full artifact includes deploy_oss.py, cert_manager.py, set_github_secret.py, build_static.py, and verify_deploy.py, so deployment, certificate, GitHub secret, build-cleanup, and verification capabilities broadly match the declared purpose.
[PE3] unexpected: Supported in part: references to .env/.npmrc/.netrc in build_static.py are exclusion safeguards, but SKILL.md and set_github_secret.py do read ~/.git-credentials for a GitHub token, which is overbroad credential reuse.
[SC2] expected: Not supported as remote code execution: the cited curl examples are deployment verification and GitHub API calls, not fetching and executing external scripts.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Supported: several triggers are broad enough to activate on generic deployment, domain binding, or HTTPS certificate requests despite the skill's Aliyun OSS-specific scope.
[AS3] expected: Not supported: the README lists this skill's expected install paths and does not instruct enumeration or reading of other installed skills.
[LP3] unexpected: Supported as a scoping concern: the skill does not separate read-only checks from mutating OSS, DNS, certificate, and GitHub operations with explicit confirmation boundaries.
[E1] expected: GitHub API calls are expected for Actions secrets and variables, but the risk is elevated because the token can be sourced implicitly from ~/.git-credentials.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only documentation and messages are apparent, but this is not a security basis for escalation by itself.
